svg.title: Data, tensor and pipeline parallel on AWS L4 GPUs
svg.desc: Three panels compare how each approach places one model across the four 24 GB L4 cards of a g6.12xlarge: data parallel copies the model, tensor parallel splits every layer, and pipeline parallel splits the model by layers. A decision strip recommends data parallel when the model fits on one card.
svg.text: On 24 GB L4 cards, model size decides how you parallelise
AWS g6.12xlarge: 4 × L4, 24 GB each. VRAM is not pooled, and the cards talk only over PCIe (64 GB/s), with no NVLink.
Each grid is one model: rows are layers, columns are slices of each layer's weights. Coloured cells are what that card holds.

Throughput up to 4×, one per card.
One engine: all 4 cards work on every step
All-reduce over PCIe, for every layer
Under 96 GB in total: each card holds
Avoid: NCCL over TCP is inefficient.
One engine: 4 stages, batches in flight
Hidden states hop once per stage
Under 96 GB in total, and every
stage must fit its own 24 GB
in flight. Each request runs no faster.

NVLink); tensor parallel as the fallback
AWS lists each L4 as 22 GiB, the same capacity as 24 GB. Sources: AWS EC2 instance-type docs, NVIDIA L4 specifications, vLLM parallelism docs (read 5 November 2026).
